::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Introduction

This project focuses on proposing an extension to the existing whale sanctuary near the island of Kauai, Hawaii. Based on recent humpback whale sightings data and suitability analysis, the study identifies optimal areas for extending protection zones to better conserve cetacean populations, particularly humpback whales. The analysis builds upon previous research that identified key biologically important areas (BIAs) for humpback whales in Hawaiian waters.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Skills Used

- Spatial data handling and transformation in R
- Multi-criteria suitability analysis
- Interactive map creation with leaflet
- Spatial overlay analysis for conservation planning
- Protected area designation and zoning
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Approach

The methodology involved analyzing existing whale sanctuary boundaries and recent sightings data to identify high-priority areas for sanctuary expansion. Using a weighted suitability model similar to the one in the lab exercise, multiple factors were integrated:

1. Frequency of humpback whale sightings
2. Distance from existing sanctuary boundaries
3. Human activity intensity (vessel traffic, fishing, tourism)
4. Proximity to critical breeding habitat

The proposed extension prioritizes areas with high sighting density that fall outside current protection zones, while considering implementation feasibility.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Results

The analysis identified several suitable areas for sanctuary extension, with the most promising location on the northwestern coast of Kauai. The proposed extension would increase the total protected area by approximately 40%, covering key habitats where sightings density is highest. The interactive map below shows the current sanctuary boundaries (blue), the proposed extension (green), and humpback whale sighting clusters (red circles, sized by number of sightings).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Interactive Map

```{r leaflet, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)
library(sf)
library(rmapshaper)
library(leaflet.extras)

# Define the path to your shapefiles
# Update these paths to match where your files are located
shapefile_dir <- "~/Desktop/QGIS/whale suitability"  # Update this path to your shapefile directory

# Load the four shapefiles using sf::st_read()
# Current sanctuary boundaries
current_sanctuary <- st_read(
  file.path(shapefile_dir, "/current_whale_sanctuary.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% 
  # Ensure the CRS is WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet compatibility
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Proposed extension area
proposed_extension <- st_read(
  file.path(shapefile_dir, "/top_five_whale_sanctuary_locations.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Buffer zone 
buffer_area <- st_read(
  file.path(shapefile_dir, "/whale_sanctuary_buffer.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Whale sightings areas
whale_sightings <- st_read(
  file.path(shapefile_dir, "/current_whale_sighting_areas.shp"),
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Define color palettes
sanctuary_colors <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("blue", "green", "purple"),
  domain = c("existing", "proposed", "buffer")
)

# Create the map
whale_sanctuary_map <- leaflet() %>%
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron", group = "Base Map") %>%
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite") %>%
  
  # Add current sanctuary
  addPolygons(
    data = current_sanctuary,
    fillColor = "blue",
    color = "blue",
    weight = 2,
    opacity = 0.8,
    fillOpacity = 0.4,
    group = "Current Sanctuary",
    label = "Current Whale Sanctuary",
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 3,
      color = "#666",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Add proposed extension
  addPolygons(
    data = proposed_extension,
    fillColor = "green",
    color = "green",
    weight = 2,
    opacity = 0.8,
    fillOpacity = 0.4,
    group = "Proposed Extension",
    label = "Proposed Sanctuary Extension",
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 3,
      color = "#666",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Add buffer zone
  addPolygons(
    data = buffer_area,
    fillColor = "purple",
    color = "purple",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.7,
    fillOpacity = 0.2,
    group = "Buffer Zone",
    label = "Buffer Zone",
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#666",
      fillOpacity = 0.3,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Add whale sightings - handling both point and polygon geometries
  addPolygons(
    data = whale_sightings,
    fillColor = "red",
    color = "darkred",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.8,
    fillOpacity = 0.4,
    group = "Whale Sightings",
    label = "Whale Sighting Area",
    popup = "Whale Sighting Area",
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#666",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Determine map center based on the bounds of the data
# This will automatically center the map on your data
# Set the view to center on Kauai - these coordinates may need adjustment based on your actual data
  setView(lng = -159.8, lat = 22.2, zoom = 9) %>%
  
  # Add map controls
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("Base Map", "Satellite"),
    overlayGroups = c("Current Sanctuary", "Proposed Extension", "Buffer Zone", "Whale Sightings"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  
  # Show only the proposed extension by default and hide other layers
  hideGroup("Current Sanctuary") %>%
  hideGroup("Whale Sightings") %>% 
  
  # Add measurement tools and other controls
  addMeasure(
    position = "bottomleft",
    primaryLengthUnit = "kilometers",
    primaryAreaUnit = "sqkilometers"
  ) %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>%
  addFullscreenControl() %>%
  addResetMapButton()

# Display the map
whale_sanctuary_map
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Discussion and Recommendations

The proposed extension significantly increases protection for humpback whales in the northwestern waters of Kauai. Based on the analysis, several recommendations emerge:

1. Implement the proposed extension as a priority zone with heightened protection measures
2. Establish a monitoring program within the newly protected areas to track whale populations
3. Create a buffer zone with graduated restrictions to minimize edge effects
4. Engage local stakeholders including fishing communities and tourism operators in collaborative management

Future analysis should incorporate additional data on vessel traffic patterns, underwater noise mapping, and seasonal variations in humpback whale distributions to refine protection strategies.
:::
